entries.technique: scheduler.yield / scheduler.postTask instead of MessageChannel posted-task yielding
entries.browserSupport: Chrome/Edge 129+, Chrome Android 129+, Firefox 142+, Safari/iOS Safari: not supported (caniuse/Chrome blog). Requires feature detection.
callSites: src/lib/quantize.js:107-114 yieldTask (fresh MessageChannel per yield, setTimeout fallback)
src/lib/palette-export.js:69 yieldExport = yieldTask

main-thread users: quantize.js (quantizeAsync 8 ms deadline), recolor.js, image-decode.js:15-28, image-reanalysis.js, onebit-usage.js, original-color-usage.js, palette-usage.js, source-color-summary.js, palette-import.js, palette-ase.js, palette-cleanup-apply.js, gif.js, save.js, App.svelte:29
worker users (yield in a dedicated worker): palette-limit.js:31, palette-generated.js:42, palette-cleanup.js:51 via palette-*-worker.js
entries.existingImplementation: Posted task (back of the task queue), 8 ms deadlines, no long-lived channel. CLAUDE.md relies on posted-task semantics: first preview slice is deferred to a posted task so many tile effects do not aggregate into one input stall.
entries.expectedBenefit: scheduler.yield continuations jump ahead of other queued same-priority tasks, so a single long job (export, Reuse) finishes sooner under contention. For the many-tile preview case this is exactly the wrong property: N tiles each yielding with boosted continuation can keep the queue busy with continuations, and Chrome only guarantees input/rendering priority heuristically. In workers the yields only service incoming messages (cancel is by terminate or 'cancel' message), so they are pure overhead, ~1 posted message per 8 ms (<~1-2%).
entries.fallback: Existing yieldTask when globalThis.scheduler?.yield is absent (Safari).
entries.correctnessAndLifetimeRisks: Changes interleaving order between concurrent tile jobs and export; Safari keeps old path so behavior diverges by engine. Abort is not tied to scheduler signals here (checkCanceled after each yield is still required).
entries.proposedMeasurement: Export-only probe: Save of a 2048 palette PNG with 6 wall tiles reconverting; compare completion time and max input delay (Event Timing) with yieldTask vs scheduler.yield in Chrome desktop + Android. Worker probe: count yields per limiter run and time with yields disabled in a Node/worker harness.

entries.existingImplementation: Every large buffer crossing a boundary is either transferred or deliberately copied in bounded 128 KiB slices because the source is shared with other consumers (wall, viewer, exports). No accidental whole-frame structured clone found.
entries.expectedBenefit: None from more transfer. The slice copies are required to keep immutable sources usable; their cost is one memcpy per byte per pass (limiter multi-pass re-sends all frames each pass).

entries.proposedMeasurement: Optional: time slice+postMessage per MiB on Android to bound the limiter's second-pass copy cost; only pursue if worker CPU traces show it above a few percent.

entries.technique: Canvas 2D usage: putImageData/drawImage/getImageData, resizing, context reuse
callSites: src/Pixels.svelte:6-11 (wall/viewer/style demos: guarded width/height, getContext('2d') each run, putImageData)
src/Tile.svelte:293,305,316 (ImageData built once per frame/size and cached in masks/colored/originals arrays)

src/lib/image-decode.js:88-104 (fallback decode: createImageBitmap -> drawImage -> getImageData, canvas zeroed in finally)
entries.existingImplementation: Tile canvases are sized to the converted sample (<= tile device pixels) and only resized when dimensions change; GIF playback reuses per-frame ImageData. Paint-only swatch canvases intentionally avoid readback (forced-dark protection). Fallback decode releases bitmap and canvas backing store.
entries.expectedBenefit: GIF playback re-uploads a full ImageData per displayed frame via putImageData; caching ImageBitmaps (createImageBitmap(ImageData) once per frame, drawImage thereafter) could avoid repeated CPU->GPU upload for looping clips. Swatch width/height reassignment on update only runs when a color changes; negligible.
entries.fallback: putImageData path stays for stills and when createImageBitmap is unavailable.
entries.correctnessAndLifetimeRisks: ImageBitmap cache adds GPU memory per frame (not covered by the 8 MiB index cache), needs close() on every invalidation, and createImageBitmap may premultiply (premultiplyAlpha default) changing displayed low-alpha RGB under Keep. Display-only, but must not drift from the export oracle. Not justified without a trace.
entries.proposedMeasurement: Trace a looping 2048 GIF on Android: if putImageData/raster upload is <5% of frame time, close the idea.

entries.correctnessAndLifetimeRisks: Adding willReadFrequently to Pixels would move wall canvases to software raster; changing colorSpace would alter displayed colors.

src/lib/tooltip.js:74-83 position(): writes maxWidth then reads two rects (one forced layout per show, acceptable)

entries.existingImplementation: measureWorkspaceTools guards most writes with value comparison (write()). CanvasGrid deliberately observes structure, not pixels.
entries.expectedBenefit: Two concrete hypotheses: (1) CanvasGrid paint rewrites three inherited custom properties on <html> after every DOM insertion/removal anywhere under #app (caption text blocks, busy notices, tile add/remove, panel open); if Blink invalidates on same-value setProperty this is a whole-document style recalc two frames later. A value guard (same pattern as App write()) would be a no-output-change fix. (2) measureWorkspaceTools forces one extra synchronous layout per run and runs on every childList mutation inside the dock, synchronously in the MutationObserver microtask; grouping all reads before writes is not trivially possible because the second read depends on the placement just written.
entries.correctnessAndLifetimeRisks: (1) Guarding is safe if the comparison uses the same serialized string. (2) Reordering can produce stale --dock-base / --panel-space and visible jumps; the code comments document a resize/show/hide feedback-loop risk.
entries.proposedMeasurement: (1) In Chrome DevTools Performance, step palettes with the dock open and count 'Recalculate style' with element count ~= whole document attributed to CanvasGrid paint; or temporary counter around root.setProperty showing calls with unchanged values. (2) Counter of measure() calls and forced-layout time per palette step / panel open.

entries.existingImplementation: Non-passive only where preventDefault is needed. However the window-level non-passive touchmove makes the whole page a blocking touch region: every touch scroll (wall, panels, dialogs) waits for the main thread before scrolling starts, so wall scrolling during a long conversion task janks on phones even though the handler returns immediately when swipe is null.

entries.correctnessAndLifetimeRisks: Pull-to-refresh / overscroll on non-wall regions would no longer be suppressed by JS (CSS overscroll-behavior could cover it but is a product change); Dock.svelte:71 'eaten' touchstart logic depends on a window capture listener. Behavior risk is real; benefit is unmeasured.
entries.proposedMeasurement: On Android, start a cold Icon 2048 conversion (known 400 ms LT) then flick-scroll a dock panel; measure scroll start latency with and without the window touchmove listener (local experiment only).

entries.technique: CompressionStream('deflate') vs fflate for PNG IDAT; ZIP assembly
entries.browserSupport: Baseline widely available since May 2023 (Chrome 80, Firefox 113, Safari 16.4); available in workers. 'deflate' is the zlib (RFC 1950) wrapper PNG requires. No compression-level option.
callSites: src/lib/save.js:1 imports fflate zipSync/zlibSync/zlib (eager in entry, 11.4 KB)
src/lib/save.js:88 legacy 1-bit pngBytes zlibSync level 3 (synchronous, byte-identical contract)
src/lib/save.js:160 palette PNG sync helper
src/lib/save.js:183-200 palettePngBytesAsync: fflate async zlib level 3 consume:true
src/lib/save.js:24-26 zipBytes zipSync level 0 (store), src/lib/save.js:273 single synchronous call over every file
entries.existingImplementation: fflate level 3. fflate's async zlib (node_modules/fflate/esm/browser.js:11-14,900-907,1446-1455) spawns a NEW classic Worker from a cached Blob URL on every call and terminates it after one result; the worker runs the same zlibSync.
entries.expectedBenefit: CompressionStream: none acceptable. It produces different encoded bytes (engine zlib at its default level, no level control), so it violates the byte-identical legacy contract and changes palette PNG bytes/sizes (decoded pixels would still match). It also would not obviously be faster than level 3. SEPARATE byte-identical candidate found while reading: for small palette PNGs (rows of a few KiB to ~64 KiB) the per-call fflate worker spawn + script eval dominates Copy/Save/hover-prepare latency; calling zlibSync(rows,{level:3}) inline below a threshold yields identical bytes because the async path runs that same function with the same options. Second: zipBytes is one synchronous CRC32 + full concatenation over the whole batch (plus Blob copy), a long task and ~2x peak memory proportional to total ZIP size.
entries.fallback: Above threshold keep the fflate worker; worker failure path unchanged.
entries.correctnessAndLifetimeRisks: Inline path is uncancelable mid-call, so threshold must keep it to ~1-2 ms on a phone. ZIP: fflate streaming Zip/ZipPassThrough or Blob-of-parts would avoid the giant buffer but may change header flags (data descriptors) and bytes; ZIP bytes already include a call-time mtime, so the oracle must be extracted-content equality, and atomicity (no download unless all succeed) must be kept.
entries.proposedMeasurement: Probe A: in Chrome desktop and Android, time palettePngBytesAsync for 16x16, 64x64, 256x256 palette images with the worker vs inline zlibSync and assert byte equality (sha256) of outputs. Probe B: time zipBytes for a 10-file 2048 batch on Android (Long Tasks) and record peak memory.

entries.technique: Per-call worker startup (module workers and fflate inline workers)
callSites: src/lib/gif.js:235 new Worker(palette-gif-worker) per palette GIF export, terminated in close()
fflate zlib per palette PNG (save.js:196)
persistent serial workers: palette-limit-client, palette-cleanup-client, palette-generated-client, image-import-client (lazily created, kept until failure)
entries.existingImplementation: Long-lived serial workers for preview stages; per-export workers for GIF/PNG compression.
entries.expectedBenefit: Per-export spawn is fixed latency (worker creation + script fetch/eval: palette-gif-worker 11 KB) that matters for tiny sprites. GIF frames are also strictly ack-serialised (gif.js:186-197): main thread converts frame i+1 only after the worker compressed frame i; one-frame-ahead pipelining would overlap main and worker CPU with identical bytes and +1 frame of memory.
entries.correctnessAndLifetimeRisks: Pipelining must preserve atomic failure, cancellation and the 'animation changed' checks; a kept-alive GIF worker would need teardown ownership.
entries.proposedMeasurement: Time Save of a 4-frame 32x32 and a 60-frame 512 GIF with performance marks around paletteGifWorker start vs first ack; for pipelining, compare total export time in Chrome/Android with byte equality.
